units.name: Magrider

tier.basis: PlanetSide 2 has no tech tiers. Main battle tanks can be pulled only at the warpgate, large outposts and major facilities (and, per the registry, away from the warpgate only while a linked Tech Plant is held); that is map control, not a tech step, so no band.

cost_band.basis: Costs the same nanites as every other main battle tank, which is the registry's cost anchor, so it sits in the medium band. Skill and facility discounts are left out.

mobility.notes: Handling is strafe rather than the hover default, drift (Handling tie-break, reason 3): players drive it, and the sources show it sliding sideways at will to dodge tank shells and infantry rockets. Next to the other empires' main battle tanks it is slower going forward (the wiki says it lacks the Prowler's pace and calls its top speed disappointing), but it alone can move sideways, and it can climb cliffs, steep ground and even buildings that stop other tanks. Magburner gives a moment of extra forward speed and lift, enough to hop over an enemy vehicle; with the Multi-directional Exhaust pick it can also steer sideways while burning. The performance-slot picks only change numbers: the Racer chassis raises forward speed and acceleration, the Rival chassis strafe speed, reverse speed and braking. It runs over soldiers in its path, friendly Engineers included.

body.notes: A low hover hull whose main cannon is built into the hull instead of a turret, so the whole tank turns to aim it; the gunner's weapon sits on its own mount on top. Coded as a fixed-gun hull for the main cannon (see fit_notes).

armour.notes: Heavy by step 3 of the armour-class order: the registry's cost anchor names the Magrider among the main battle tanks. Directional armour shared by every main battle tank: shots from the side do a little more, from behind half again as much, and from below double. Melee, small arms, splash damage and flak bursts do nothing to it; heavy machine guns, anti-aircraft guns and gatling rounds do only a small part; tank shells do half again as much, and C4, anti-vehicle grenades and tank mines double. Below a fifth of its health it catches fire and burns, as every vehicle does. Self-repair comes from the Nanite Auto Repair System, a defense-slot pick that has been the default fitting since the September 2021 update. The other defense picks only trim damage: Flanker Armor against C4, soldiers' rocket launchers and the warheads aircraft fire at the ground, Mine Guard against tank mines. The wiki rates its front armour below the Vanguard's.

sensors.notes: PlanetSide 2 has no fog of war, so the sight band is the medium proposal. No sensor comes with every loadout. Defense-slot picks: Proximity Radar shows nearby enemy soldiers on the minimap, for the tank's own crew only; Vehicle Stealth slows enemy lock-ons and shortens the range at which the tank shows up on enemy minimaps by itself, removing it at the top rank. Every weapon can take thermal or night-vision optics.

armament.name: Supernova PC (also Supernova FPC and Supernova VPC)
armament.summary: The driver's plasma cannon, fixed in the hull and aimed by turning the tank. Each shot is a travelling plasma charge that bursts where it lands, with a short wait between shots that is quicker than on the other empires' tank guns. The stock PC (the HEAT choice) is the all-rounder; the FPC (AP) flies faster and hits vehicles harder with less blast; the VPC (HESH) gives up damage to armour for a wider blast that kills soldiers. Its tank-shell damage does extra to vehicles and far more to aircraft. Recruiter and Fafnir copies are the same guns.

armament.name: Perihelion VXC
armament.summary: A prototype hull cannon built against armour. Its wide crescent shots fly dead straight with no drop, so it stays accurate very far out. Holding the trigger charges it so that one release sends out two or three crescents in a quick burst, each using a round of its small magazine.

armament.name: M20 Basilisk (also V42 Pariah and M12 Kobalt)
armament.summary: The gunner's heavy machine guns on the top mount. The Basilisk, free and shared by every empire's tanks, chips at any target; the Pariah, a free Vanu version, fires glowing plasma bolts but counts as a heavy machine gun and holds its accuracy further out; the Kobalt, a cheap pick, fires infantry-type rounds that shred soldiers but barely touch armour. Tanks and other heavy vehicles shrug off most of what these guns do.

armament.name: G30 Walker
armament.summary: An anti-aircraft heavy machine gun shared by the three empires' tanks: very fast soft-point rounds and a steep upward reach, with no fuse or lock, so every round must hit. Strong against aircraft and still usable against soft ground targets; ground vehicles resist most of its damage.

armament.name: G40-F Ranger
armament.summary: A flak cannon for air defence, shared by the three empires' tanks: its shells burst when they pass close to enemy aircraft, so near misses still hurt. Its direct hits do little to anything on the ground, and ground vehicles ignore the flak burst entirely.

armament.name: E540 Halberd
armament.summary: A single-shot armour-piercing rocket launcher shared by the three empires' tanks: one heavy, fairly fast rocket with a small blast, then a reload, so it hits hard per shot but less over time. A Halberd SE copy with a plasma look works the same.

armament.name: Saron HRB (also Proton II PPA)
armament.summary: Two Vanu top guns that fire travelling energy bolts which burst on impact. The Saron HRB sends fast, precise anti-vehicle bolts from a short magazine, its aim spreading for a moment after every shot; the Proton II PPA throws big, slow plasma balls that explode where they hit, with a wide blast for clusters of soldiers and light vehicles.

armament.name: Aphelion VEX-4
armament.summary: An experimental Vanu energy chain gun built for close fights with vehicles. It fires faster the longer the trigger stays down, and sustained fire stores leftover energy that it can let go as a crescent wave: one heavy hit that reaches further and passes through up to two targets. Letting go of the trigger resets the spin.

crew.notes: Two operating seats in the source: the driver fires the hull-fixed main cannon, and a gunner fires the top gun (the game's certification lines split its weapons into primary and gunner weapons). Alone, the driver keeps the main cannon; the top gun waits for a teammate. No passenger seats.

abilities.name: Magburner
abilities.summary: Hold the boost key to burn a small fuel tank for a moment of extra forward speed and acceleration; the wiki adds that it lifts the hover, so the tank can hop over an enemy vehicle to reach its weak rear armour or cross small gaps. The fuel refills by itself, faster at ranks bought with certification points. Built in at its first rank since the August 2019 update.

abilities.name: Fire Suppression System
abilities.summary: Utility pick, fitted by default since the September 2021 update: press to restore part of the tank's health over a few seconds and, if it is burning, put the fire out.

abilities.name: Smoke Screen
abilities.summary: Utility pick: puts out smoke around the tank for a few seconds. While it lasts, the tank and allied vehicles close by drop off enemy minimaps (no automatic detection) and cannot be locked onto.

abilities.name: Recharge
abilities.summary: Magrider-only utility pick: refills the Magburner fuel at once and throws off any lock-on being made on the tank.

abilities.name: Multi-directional Exhaust
abilities.summary: Magrider-only defense pick: Magburner refills faster, and the driver can steer sideways while it burns instead of being pushed almost straight ahead.

on_death.notes: Players drive it in a game where they respawn after dying; whoever is still inside when it is destroyed dies with it, unless they jumped out by hand first.

strengths.why: As a hover tank it slides sideways, so it can dodge incoming tank shells and infantry rockets, and it rides over most rough ground.
Climbs cliffs, steep slopes and even buildings that other tanks cannot, finding firing angles the enemy does not expect.
Magburner can hop it over an enemy vehicle to shoot that vehicle's weak rear armour, or carry it away from missiles and shells.
Suits long-range duels: its cannon reaches far while its strafe dodges return fire.
Main battle tank armour: small arms, melee, splash damage and flak do nothing to it.

weaknesses.why: Its main cannon is fixed in the hull, so the whole tank has to turn to aim, and on flat ground it struggles to point up at aircraft.
The wiki ranks it last of the three empires' tanks on paper: its cannon hits less hard than the Prowler's twin guns or the Vanguard's big gun.
Thinner at the front than the Vanguard, and it takes more from the sides, much more from behind and the most from below.
Its forward top speed is a letdown for a tank, and the Prowler outruns it.
Its top gun needs a second player; a lone driver has only the hull-fixed cannon.

countered_by.why: C4, anti-vehicle grenades and tank mines do double damage to it; a Heavy Assault soldier needs only two bricks of C4 to destroy it.
Head-on, the other empires' main battle tanks out-armour and out-gun it; it wins only by dodging at range or flanking to their sides and rear.
The wiki names the Vanguard as having heavier front armour and a bigger gun, so it wins a frontal duel with the Magrider.
The hull-fixed cannon aims badly upward; against aircraft overhead it needs a slope or rock to tilt the tank.

counters.why: Its tank-shell damage hits lighter vehicles hard, and the wiki sends it to clear the vehicles guarding a facility.
The wiki uses it to knock out the turrets that defend a Tech Plant or an Amp Station.
Its plasma charges burst among soldiers, it reaches angles infantry cannot cover, and it runs over those who stay standing.

combos.why: Engineers repair it in the field, though they must stay alert because its sideways drift can run them over.

units.memorable: The hover tank with its cannon built into the hull: it slides sideways to dodge shells, climbs cliffs and buildings, and can burn its thrusters to hop over an enemy tank.
units.as_player: You drive and fire the hull-fixed plasma cannon on left mouse, aiming by turning the whole tank: strafe sideways to dodge shells, climb slopes other tanks can't, and hold Shift for a short Magburner surge, even over an enemy tank to hit its rear. F fires your utility pick (repair, smoke or Recharge). A second player in the gunner seat aims the free-turning top gun: a heavy machine gun by default, or an anti-air, rocket or plasma pick. Alone, the top gun stays silent.

sources.title: Magrider, PlanetSide 2 Wiki
sources.version: Main tab current to the 30 March 2022 update
sources.note: Read through its Main, Weapons and History tabs (the subpages Magrider/Main, Magrider/Weapons and Magrider/History). The Main tab's infobox description copies the game's own vehicle description, which the Census entry below gives directly. The Weapons tab lists every main cannon and top-gun choice one by one, with its effective-range word, muzzle velocity, blast and whether it comes free.

sources.title: Magrider vehicle entry with its slot items and certification lines, Daybreak Census API
sources.note: The developer's public game-data service: the vehicle collection's description of the Magrider, joined with the vehicle_attachment and item collections (the game's own text for every weapon and slot item, with the cooldowns of each rank), the vehicle_skill_set and skill_set collections (which weapons are primary and which are gunner weapons) and the skill collection (Magburner ranks). It still lists a few old slot items (ECM Suite and Reinforced Front, Side and Top Armor) that the wiki's current certification list no longer has.

sources.title: Vehicle armor and damage resistance, PlanetSide 2 Wiki
sources.note: Its resist table gives each vehicle's resistance to each damage category, whose names list, on hover, the weapons that use them; its directional table gives the main battle tanks' side, rear and underside values.

uncertain.note: No page read gives the Magrider's forward speed as a figure (the wiki gives no vehicle top speeds, and its patch notes give only changes, such as a 2018 increase). Fast is a judgement: a main battle tank clearly outpaces a sprinting soldier, and the wiki finds the Magrider's top speed poor and slower than the Prowler's. It could be very fast if its top speed is somewhat higher than assumed.
Step 4 reads the resist table: the tank-shell category of the stock cannon does extra damage to vehicles, and even more to aircraft, but anti-air was skipped because no stock weapon reaches high air.

Channel rests on the wiki's Afterburner page (read, not cited for lack of room), which says the burn stops the moment the key is let go or the tank is empty; the Magburner page, also read, says to press and hold the key. The cited pages only say the boost is brief.

Banded from the first rank's refill time from empty to full, which the cited Census text and the wiki's Magburner and Afterburner pages agree on. For the higher ranks the Census text and the wiki's August 2019 patch summary give different refill times.

Two top guns come free: the M20 Basilisk and the V42 Pariah (added in March 2022). The Basilisk's own wiki page (read, not cited) calls it the stock top gun of every empire's tanks, so it is named first; both fall in this one entry either way.
Plasma rather than cannon: the game calls the shots plasma charges and the registry note treats Vanu bolt weapons as plasma, but the gun fights like a tank cannon (one heavy shot, then a pause).

Ranges come from the wiki's effective-range words (Long, Very Long, Medium, Close), as the registry's range reference says; no page gives a maximum reach. Deliveries are projectile because every gun has a muzzle velocity on the Weapons tab, though no page describes the flight in words.

Each weapon's own wiki page was read but not cited for lack of room. They give each gun's damage category (also shown on the cited resistance page), the game's description (also in the cited Census entry) and the prose used in the summaries: the Aphelion's crescent wave, the Perihelion's charge, the Walker and Ranger compared with each other, the Kobalt against armour and the Halberd's single shot.

The Aphelion's chain-gun fire is rated Close and its crescent wave Medium-Long on its own page; medium was chosen as the band for its longest reach, since Medium-Long sits between our medium and long.

How the crescent wave is released and that it pierces up to two targets come from the Aphelion's own page (read, not cited); the cited Census text only says sustained fire builds energy that can be let out as a blast.
Magazine was left off: the Perihelion's small magazine and reload appear only in a stats table, and no cited page describes it stopping to reload as part of how it fights.

The Ranger's direct hits can still scratch ground vehicles (its direct-hit category is the heavy machine gun one, which tanks mostly resist), but the flak family leaves ground vehicles out, so only infantry is listed on the ground.
Fixed-gun hull or hull with turret: the main cannon is fixed in the hull like a tank destroyer's, but a turret on top carries the gunner's weapon.
No cited page describes what happens when it is destroyed; respawn follows the rule for vehicles players drive in a game where they come back.
Anti-air rests only on option top guns (the Walker and the Ranger); the stock loadout cannot reach high air.

The Census entry still lists ECM Suite (the same text as Smoke Screen) and three Reinforced Armor plates; the wiki's current certification list for the Magrider has none of them, so they are left out.

fit_notes.wanted: a fixed-gun hull that also carries a gunner's turret
fit_notes.note: The main cannon is fixed in the hull, but the gunner's weapon sits on a turret on top. Neither the fixed-gun hull (no turret) nor the hull with turret (the main gun in the turret) describes this.
The hover term says hover units avoid steep slopes; the Magrider is the opposite, climbing cliffs and buildings other tanks cannot. No cited page says whether it crosses water.

fit_notes.wanted: a pattern for a pick that reshapes another ability, here a dash that can strafe
fit_notes.note: Multi-directional Exhaust lets the driver steer sideways during Magburner and refills it faster; it is not a dash of its own, so dash is not linked.

fit_notes.wanted: refill your own boost or ability charge on a key
fit_notes.note: Recharge both breaks lock-ons and refills the Magburner fuel; only the first part has a pattern.

fit_notes.wanted: fuel, for a boost gauge that refills by itself
fit_notes.note: Magburner burns a small fuel tank that refills by itself over time anywhere; the fuel term describes a gauge refilled on the ground or at a pad, so it is left out and the gauge is read as the boost's limit.

atypical.note: The game's own description and the wiki both say the Magrider climbs terrain other tanks cannot, up cliffs and even buildings; our word list keeps climbing for infantry, walkers and drones.
The same climbing, on a hover tank: our word list allows climb only on foot or on many legs, and its hover term even says hover units avoid steep slopes.
The main cannon is fixed in the hull, but the gunner's top weapons sit on their own free-turning mount; the fixed-gun hull allows only body-aim or limited-arc mounts.
